correctness.rationale: For a pair of square-zero endomorphisms of dimension \(4r\) with equal images of AB and BA of rank \(r\), the common image U is annihilated by both factors. Restricting B to im A and A to im B forces each rank \(2r\) and then ker A=im A, ker B=im B. Their intersection is precisely U and the two products induce isomorphisms from V/(im A+im B) to U. A four-block basis yields canonical matrices indexed by H in GL_r. The simultaneous centralizer has \(q^{3r^2}|C_{\mathrm{GL}_r(q)}(H)|\) elements; orbit-stabilizer followed by the complete conjugacy-class mass identity gives \(|\mathrm{GL}_{4r}(q)|/q^{3r^2}\). The fixed-first-factor identity follows by dividing by the Gaussian count of rank-\(2r\) square-zero matrices. Exhaustive checks: binary dimension-four pairs 2520, ternary second-factor count 144, dimension-eight centralizer dimensions 16/14/14 for three test parameters. Finite experiments do not replace the all-field proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed contribution is the exact arithmetic mass of the sharp common-product-image locus and its fixed-first-factor fibers, not the rank inequality or generic band-module parameterization. Mohammadian proves the inequality and Crawley-Boevey classifies modules for the full square-zero-pair algebra, but the inspected available material does not directly state these rank-saturation counts or the stabilizer cancellation. A derivation hidden in the full inaccessible inequality paper, or a finite-field automorphism-mass calculation implicit in general string/band classifications, remains a specific priority risk; absence from a search is not treated as proof.

The stabilizer parameters cancel across all rational similarity classes, yielding unexpectedly simple counts for both total pairs and the fiber over a fixed first operator. The object and invariant arise from a published extremal bound, not an arbitrary parameter choice.
